script:
Punjabi (Gurmukhi), Shree-Lipi 7 family. Composers: S8PunU64.dll (Unicode, TutorGetMappedCodeW) and S8Pun764.dll (Shree-Lipi 7 raw bytes, TutorGetMappedCode). Both answer for Punjabi, even though Shree's Converter returns nothing for Punjabi 7.

This is the retry. The earlier run of this same task (identical prompt) finished every capture step before the workflow failed elsewhere on network errors (ENOTFOUND). The pipeline is resumable and its files are intact, so this round did not capture everything again. It re-checked the results and added three things.

What this round checked:
- The shipped tables and the converter code are unchanged since the measure. md5 of unicode-to-shree-pun7.json is 1fafc715…, of shree-pun7-to-unicode.json 2c4c593f…; FontConverter.cs and MappingTable.cs are identical in the main checkout, snap-base and the build copy repo/.
- Stability, recomputed from the raw captures (verify-r2.js): every capture's run A and run B are byte-identical.
- measure.exe was run again and wrote measure.json, forward-failures.tsv and reverse-failures.tsv byte-identical to the first run.
- **Correction to the earlier report:** the 12 vendor captures (capvo/) were taken with the first probe, before the "#loaded" check existed, so they have no #loaded line. I proved instead that each load took:
  - every keyboard's layer-0 single-code keys answer exactly as the same code does on the raw-code layer (CRTRONIC 71/71, DOE 64/64, GODREJ 72/72, INSCRIPT 70/70, ITR 78/78, RAMING 78/78, ROMA 72/72, TYPEWRIT 78/78, VARITYPE 74/74; ENG 64/65, PHONETIC 63/64, NEWROMA 71/73, the misses being their phonetic modes);
  - the 12 keyboards give 12 different sets of answers.

What this round added:
1. **Nesting test** (pn/QAAA.PUN → capn/QAAA.tsv): can a slot hold a reference to another slot, so one key types more than 4 codes? No. Both composers ignore a slot reference (B0-CE) inside a slot:
   - [ref] alone types nothing; [ref][ref] types nothing;
   - [ref] + ੰ gives just ੰ (A5);
   - ਕ + [ref] gives just ਕ (48).
   So no key can probe more than 4 codes.
2. **Reverse measured over every spelling Shree types**, not only the preferred one (revall/).
3. **Evidence for the C੍C policy:** 10 of 12 vendor keyboards put the halant code 44 (visible B5) on their virama key. Only NEWROMA '=' and ROMA 'f' carry the link code 64, which writes no glyph.

SLNXT (running since 00:59):
- SL8_DLL_DATA had changed since the first run's restore at 03:05: header byte 2 = 01, tables all zero. Someone else changed it, not this agent.
- I saved that state (shmdump/now-r2.bin, and nestexp-pre.bin just before the one composer run), wrote it back afterwards with probe2 --put (0 bytes differ, safe-run.log), and checked again at the end: final-r2.bin equals now-r2.bin.
- One composer process at a time; probe keyboards in neutral 8.3 paths. No UI, typing, clipboard, Word or dotnet build was used in this round.

stability:
Every capture was run twice, in separate probe processes. I recomputed the comparison from the raw files in this round (verify-r2-stability.json):
- vendor keyboards: 12/12 identical (capvo vs capvo-b);
- P: 786/786 identical;
- H: 425/425 identical;
- S: 31/31 identical.

Within each run, probe2 asks every key twice, and every file has #stable 1.

Load checks:
- Every probe file has #loaded 1: table 0 of SL8_DLL_DATA equalled the keyboard file after LoadKbdOverlay.
- The untouched ITR check keys (V X Z : ; 0 5) answered correctly in all 1,242 probe files.
- The vendor files have no #loaded line. Their loads are proven by the per-key match with the raw-code layer, and by each of the 12 keyboards giving different answers.
- The composers re-captured ITR.BAN byte-identical to the 11 Oct Bangla capture.

Quirks:
- No "Lk"/"Hf" placeholders, and no answer given to many keys at once.
- The Unicode composer puts a carrier before a lone sign: a leading space (13,919 answers) or a '.' before ਿ (1,270). 44 answers end in a NUL (ਇ comes back as 0A07 0000).
- The 7 composer returns -256 (nothing) in 3,791 answers. 18 phonetic-keyboard answers sit on carrier byte 07, which no font has.
- The phonetic keyboards (ENG, NEWROMA, PHONETIC, ROMA) answer a consonant as C + ੍, and their bindi key types tippi.

Unicode composer rules, accepted in the truth:
- A tippi typed after ਾ ੀ ੇ ੈ ੋ ੌ ਉ ਊ ੳ is written as bindi U+0A02 (984 canonical rows). The 7 bytes equal the bindi probes.
- ੱ followed by ਂ is written as ਁ U+0A01 (49 rows).
- ੴ is U+0A74.

Unicode composer quirks, kept out of the truth (954 rows):
- ਡ + nukta is written ੜ.
- ਓ + ੁ is written ਉ.
- With ਿ struck late, the i-sign is moved.

7 composer quirks:
- It loses the addak after ੀ/ੇ/ੈ/ੌ + ਂ (6 rows).
- On ਠ/ਨ it loses a vowel sign or a subjoined glyph (the gaps above).
- It drops “ ” ॥ ੴ(E0) ਇ(E4).

Layer alignment:
- Both composers answer the Ctrl+Space layer and the raw-code layer by the code the key holds: layer 1 agrees on 124/124 keys, the raw-code layer on 570/584. The 14 misses are the phonetic modes.
- The composer keeps no state between calls: the check keys answer the same after any preceding key.

Nesting test, this round: a slot reference inside a slot is ignored by both composers.
family:
One table serves both families, except ₹.

How the fonts were compared (fontcmp.js, with my own TTF reader, rendering by glyph index to avoid the 0xAD trap):
- 7: WPUN7001.TTF (SHREE-PUN7-0951) and WPUN7002.TTF (SHREE-PUN7-0952). Each has a (3,1) format-4 cmap with 119 codes and 123 glyphs.
- 4/5/6: S09500F2, S09510F2, S09520F2, S09550F2 and S09560F2.TTF (SHREE-PUN-0950/0951/0952/0955/0956). Each has 118 codes and 122 glyphs.
- I checked C:\Windows\Fonts again this round: these are the only Punjabi 7 and 4/5/6 faces installed. S09xx810 are the PUNX (Ex) family, and S0960/62/64892 are SHREE-SAN7.

Results:
- Same design, 0951 (WPUN7001 vs S09510F2) and 0952 (WPUN7002 vs S09520F2): 118 of 119 codes have identical glyf bytes and advances. The one difference is 3C (₹), which only the 7 faces have.
- All five 4/5/6 faces map the same 118 codes to the same glyph ids; both 7 faces map the same 119.
- Every byte in the truth exists in every face, except 3C, which the 4/5/6 faces lack (bytesInTruthNotInAnyFont = []).
- No face has 07 (the phonetic carrier) or 78/7B/80-9F/C0+.
- languages.json already wires all 7 Punjabi faces to shree-pun7. That is right; for a 4/5/6 face, ₹ must be dropped or reported.

Glyphs identified from the renders:
- B0 is the onkar arc without the ੧; the full ੴ is 31 B0.
- A7 is the addak over the letter; A8 is the addak further right, after top marks and after ਉ/ਊ/ੳ.
- A4 is the bindi to the right of ਉ/ਊ; 44 is ੳ + bindi.
- 73 7A 7C 7E A2 are the sign + bindi ligatures for ੀ ੇ ੈ ੋ ੌ.
- BE is a spacer (advance 120) that follows ਠ (53) and ਨ (B2).
- AE/AF are ੁ/ੂ for use after BE.
- 6E is the ਕ੍ਰ ligature.
- 6F, AA, AB and 62 are the subjoined ੍ਰ ੍ਹ ੍ਵ ੍ਯ.
- B5 is the halant.
currentTables:
What was measured: unicode-to-shree-pun7.json (238 pairs, 1 preRule) and shree-pun7-to-unicode.json (93 pairs), run through the real FontConverter built from the snapshot copy. These files are identical to the main checkout's. I re-ran the measure this round and its output was byte-identical.
- The product path is the same table: ConversionPipeline and MainViewModel both call CreateConverterToLegacy("shree-pun7"), and TypingEngine.RerenderLegacy runs ConvertText on the Unicode word. So the forward failures below also appear when typing in a Shree-PUN font.
- The product's Unicode output additionally goes through Nukta.Spell, which writes nukta letters decomposed. That is canonically the same text.

Forward (Unicode → bytes):
- Exact: 25,260/27,752 = 91.02%.
- Accepted: also 91.02%. Whenever ours is right it is Shree's preferred spelling (B5 for C੍C).
- 2,492 strings fail; 7 of those match a Shree alternative.
- 141 rows report unmapped characters: ਁ 46, ZWJ 38, ZWNJ 38, ₹ 1, and 18 ASCII characters that pass through correctly.
- The same strings in NFC form (nukta decomposed): 1,086/1,146 exact.
- 20,000 random joined words: 75.58% exact, with no effect across syllables.
- Common Punjabi words: 198/238 exact (measured/common-words.tsv). Wrong ones include ਨੂੰ ਨੇ ਇੱਕ ਇਹ ਇਸ ਉੱਤੇ ਉੱਚਾ ਉੱਥੇ ਇੱਥੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਤੁਹਾਨੂੰ ਸਾਨੂੰ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਨੌਂ ਨੰਬਰ ਬਠਿੰਡਾ ਕੈਨੇਡਾ ਇੰਗਲੈਂਡ ੴ ₹.
- For contrast, the tables' own round trip is 27,751/27,752 = 100.00%. That is the green-test figure.

Forward failure categories (Unicode: ours | Shree):
1. **Addak must be A8, not A7,** after ੀ ੇ ੈ ੋ ੌ ਂ ੰ and after ਉ ਊ ੳ: 887 strings. ਉੱ 45 A7 | 45 A8 (affects ਉੱਤੇ, ਉੱਚਾ); ਕੀੱ 48 72 A7 | 48 72 A8; ਕਂੱ 48 A3 A7 | 48 A3 A8.
2. **Spacer BE after ਠ/ਨ,** about 1,100 strings:
   - BE missing before a subjoined form (428): ਨ੍ਹ B2 AA | B2 BE AA; ਠ੍ਰ 53 6F | 53 BE 6F.
   - Top marks written after BE instead of before it (546): ਨੇ B2 BE 79 | B2 79 BE; ਨੂੰ B2 BE 76 A5 | B2 A5 BE 76; ਨੰ B2 BE A5 | B2 A5 BE; ਠੱ 53 BE A7 | 53 A7 BE; ਨੌ B2 BE A1 | B2 A1 BE.
   - ੁ ੂ after BE must be AE/AF (136): ਨੁ B2 BE 74 | B2 BE AE; ਨੂ B2 BE 76 | B2 BE AF.
   - ਠ/ਨ + subjoined + sign: ਠ੍ਰੇ 53 6F 79 | 53 79 BE 6F.
3. **The i-sign is not moved in front of ੜ, the nukta letters U+0A59-0A5E, ੲ, ਅ, ੳ or ਓ,** about 86 strings. The preRule only covers U+0A15-0A39. ਇ 42 71 | 71 42 (breaks ਇਹ ਇਸ ਇੱਕ); ਖ਼ਿ 69 71 | 71 69; ੜਿ 6D 71 | 71 6D; ੜ੍ਕਿ 6D B5 71 48 | 71 6D B5 48.
4. **ZWJ/ZWNJ passed through:** 76 strings. ਕ੍‍ 48 B5 U+200D | 48; ਕ੍‌ 48 B5 U+200C | 48 B5.
5. **ਁ U+0A01 unmapped:** 41 strings. ਕਁ 48 U+0A01 | 48 A7 A3.
6. **Bindi ligatures on independent vowels:** ਈਂ 42 72 A3 | 42 73; ਏਂ 42 79 A3 | 42 7A; ਐਂ 41 B1 A3 | 41 7C; ਔਂ 41 A1 A3 | 41 A2; ਊਂ 46 A3 | 46 A4; ੳਂ 43 A3 | 44.
7. ੴ: B0 | 31 B0.
8. ₹: U+20B9 | 3C (7 faces only).

Reverse (Shree's preferred bytes → Unicode):
- Exact: 26,627/27,752 = 95.95%.
- Same text: 26,718 = 96.27%.
- All accepted spellings, same text: 27,870/47,157 = 59.10%. Allowing for the virama the link spelling cannot show: 43,782/47,157 = 92.84%.
- 874 rows read unmapped bytes: BE 695, AF 81, AE 80, 3C 1, plus ASCII.

Reverse failure categories:
1. A standalone BE, AE or AF is read as ¾, ® or ¯ (856). B2 79 BE gives ਨੇ¾; B2 A5 BE 76 gives ਨੰ¾ੂ; B2 BE AE gives ਨ®.
2. 71 before ੜ or a nukta letter is not reordered (about 90). 71 6D gives ਿੜ, should be ੜਿ.
3. 48 A7 A3 reads ਕੱਂ, but the Unicode composer writes ਕਁ (44).
4. 31 B0 reads ੧ੴ; should be ੴ.
5. 3C reads '<'; should be ₹.
6. 44 reads ੳ; should be ੳਂ.

New this round, the reverse table over every other spelling Shree types (revall/): 24,581 non-preferred spellings.
- 3,874 read back as the same text.
- 20,126 cannot, because the link code writes no virama glyph, so the bytes are the plain letters. Examples: 48 63 is ਕਰ for ਕ੍ਰ; 71 49 48 is ਖਿਕ for ਖ੍ਕਿ; 48 48 B5 is ਕਕ੍.
- 580 are the known bugs: 576 BE/AE/AF read as ¾ ® ¯, and 4 with the i-sign before ੜ (71 6D B5 63 gives ਿੜ੍ਰ).
- 1 is a composer quirk (44 A3 for ੳਂਂ).
- No new failure category.
keyboards:
All 12 shipped Punjabi keyboards are captured key by key from their original paths (C:\Shree-Lipi nxt\*.PUN), in both composers (U and 7). Each was captured twice in separate processes (byte-identical), and each run asked every key twice. MODULAR exists only as a chart and has no .PUN file.

Layers captured:
- Layer 0, the printed keyboard (normal and shift are separate ASCII keys): 1,031 answered keys.
- Layer 1, Ctrl+Space: 151.
- Layer 2, the composer's raw code layer (key character = internal code; layers 3-12 answer the same): 1,004.

Per keyboard (layer 0/1/2): CRTRONIC 87/16/83, DOE 77/21/83, ENG 81/12/87, GODREJ 81/18/83, INSCRIPT 89/6/83, ITR 92/12/83, NEWROMA 82/13/83, PHONETIC 81/12/87, RAMING 89/8/83, ROMA 85/16/83, TYPEWRIT 93/10/83, VARITYPE 94/7/83.

Where the data is:
- Raw captures: capvo\*.tsv (run A) and capvo-b\*.tsv (run B).
- Compiled: pun-vendor-keys.json. For every key and layer it gives the codes the key holds (conjunct slot expanded, in typed order), the raw Unicode answer in hex, the cleaned Unicode, and the 7 bytes.
- The Ctrl+Shift+1 symbol layer cannot be reached through the tutor. Its section (ctrlShift1) comes from the charts plus each code's composer answer: $ → EF → ₹ / 3C, * → DC → × / 23, / → DD → ÷ / 24.

Notes for a later per-key audit:
- Keys holding code 51 type ੴ as B0 alone, the arc without the ੧. These are the Ctrl+Space q key on ITR, DOE, CRTRONIC, GODREJ, RAMING and ROMA, plus others. VARITYPE key O types 31 B0.
- RAMING key P (codes 31 42 4D) types ੧ੳ = 31 43.
- The phonetic keyboards answer consonants as C੍, the bindi key as tippi A5, and lone signs on byte 07.
- The virama key holds the halant code 44 (B5) on 10 keyboards. NEWROMA '=' and ROMA 'f' hold the link code 64, which writes no glyph.
notes:
What still blocks a perfect table:

(1) Shree's own 7 composer has no usable answer for 83 strings (pun7-composer-gaps.json). Among them is ਨ੍ਹਾਂ, which appears in very common words (ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ, ਜਿਨ੍ਹਾਂ, ਇਨ੍ਹਾਂ). 36 of the 83 have a spelling derived from the composer's rules (ਨ੍ਹਾਂ → B2 BE AA 70 A3; typed bindi-first, Shree itself writes B2 A3 BE AA 70). The 47 with ੁ/ੂ + tail on ਠ/ਨ + subjoined have no single answer.

(2) More than 4 codes cannot be probed. A slot holds 4 codes and slot references inside a slot are ignored (shown this round). The DLLs export only TutorGetMappedCode(W), TutorGetAkshar, TutorGetAlterCode, GetAksharCount(W), SET_AKSHAR, LoadKbdOverlay and the hook procs (pe-exports.js). Feeding keys through the hook procs would type into the foreground window, so I did not try it.

(3) Policy choices the composer cannot settle:
- C੍C before a letter with no subjoined form. The halant spelling B5 is preferred (10/12 vendor virama keys type it); the link spelling (no glyph) is accepted.
- ੴ: 31 B0 (preferred) against B0 (what 11 vendor keys type).
- ॥, “ and ” have no 7 spelling at all.
- ਁ against ੱ + ਂ.
- ₹ exists in the 7 faces only.
- The legacy-only codes 41 → 40 and EE → A9 have no Unicode identity.

(4) Udaat ੑ and yakash ੵ have no code at all.

(5) The table must take nukta letters both precomposed and in NFC form.

Fix priorities, by word frequency:
1. BE ordering and AE/AF for ਠ/ਨ, in both directions. Reverse prints ¾, ® or ¯ into any Shree document that has ਨ/ਠ + a mark.
2. A8 after ਉ and after the top signs (ਉੱਤੇ).
3. The i-sign reorder for ੲ/ੜ/nukta letters (ਇ).
4. Drop ZWJ/ZWNJ.
5. Add ਁ, ੴ, ₹ and the independent-vowel bindi ligatures.

TypingEngine: not measured key by key. Legacy typing runs the same forward table, so its failures carry over. pun-vendor-keys.json is ready for a per-key audit without the composer.

Memory note candidates:
- The Punjabi tutor has no Ctrl+Shift+1 layer; layers 2 and up are the raw code table. Both composers answer Ctrl+Space and the raw-code layer aligned.
- A slot reference inside a conjunct slot is ignored, so one key can never type more than 4 codes.
- SLNXT's SL8_DLL_DATA can hold no keyboard (tables zero, header byte 2 = 00 or 01). Restore it by writing the saved dump back (probe2 --put), not with LoadKbdOverlay.
